transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I don’t feel any interest in the things I used to love—my art, my garden, even time with my family just feels flat. I just feel so weary and empty, and I don't know why I can't seem to care about anything anymore.
How long have you been feeling this way? Has this been going on for a few weeks or months, or has it been a constant feeling for several years?

It’s been building up and sticking around for a little over two years now. It really started when my husband began traveling more for work and the kids became more independent, leaving me alone at home for long stretches. Since then, this flat feeling has just persisted.
During these past two years, have you had any periods lasting more than two months where your mood returned to normal and you felt like your usual self?

No, I haven't really had a period where I felt completely back to my usual self. There was a stretch last year where my mood felt relatively neutral, but I was still hearing those whispers and feeling convinced my family was testing me. So even when my mood wasn't high or low, it still didn't feel like a true return to normal.
How long did that period last where your mood felt neutral but you were still hearing those whispers and having those thoughts about your family?

That neutral stretch lasted for about two or three weeks. Even though I wasn't feeling especially high or low during those weeks, the whispering late at night and the feeling that my family was testing me kept happening just the same.
When did the whispers and the feeling that your family is testing you first begin? Did they start around the same time you began feeling empty and down, or did one start before the other?

The whispers and the feeling of being tested actually started first, about a year and a half ago. The heavy, empty, and down feelings came much later, and have only really been a problem for about seven months in total.
Have you ever experienced periods where you felt the exact opposite of down—such as feeling unusually energetic, hyperactive, or needing very little sleep?

Yes, I do have stretches where I feel completely wired and buzzing with energy, easily getting by on just three or four hours of sleep without feeling tired. During those times, I talk fast, get easily annoyed, and rush around starting a dozen different projects like reorganizing the house or planning art programs.
How long do these periods of feeling wired and high-energy typically last, and how often do they occur?

Those wired phases have been coming and going for close to a year and eight months now. When I look back, they actually take up the majority of the time compared to my low stretches, even though they come and go in waves.
Have you ever experienced the whispers or the feeling of being tested for a longer period—say, a month or more—during which your mood was completely stable, without feeling wired or down?

Yes, I've had that happen, though it wasn't quite a month—it was that stretch of about two or three weeks last year. Even though my mood felt completely stable and neutral, I still heard the whispering at night and remained convinced my husband's trips were part of a test.
During that two to three week period when your mood was neutral, were the whispers and the belief that you were being tested just as strong as they are during your high or low periods?

Yes, they were absolutely just as strong and felt completely real to me. Even though my mood wasn't high or low during those weeks, the whispers and the feeling of being tested didn't fade or change at all.
When you are not experiencing those high or low mood phases, do the whispers and the feeling of being tested ever go away completely, or do they continue to linger?

They definitely continue to linger. Even during that stretch last year when my mood was completely neutral, I still heard the whispering at night and remained convinced that my husband's work trips were part of a test on me.
Have you or those close to you noticed any times where your speech became jumbled, or where you had significant trouble organizing your thoughts and expressing them clearly to others?

Yes, that happens a lot when I try to explain what's going on in my head. I might start talking about my garden, but then I'll suddenly jump to money or my kids' future, and halfway through I'll completely forget what you even asked me. It just feels like my thoughts are sliding off in different directions and I can't keep them on track.
Can you tell me more about the whispers you hear? Do they sound like distinct voices talking to each other, or a voice commenting on what you are doing?

Yes, it sounds like a man and a woman whispering my name from the hallway or the garden late at night. They comment on how I'm doing as a mother, almost like they are judging my parenting. Even though I know there is no one actually there, it still feels incredibly real when it happens.
Have you been using any recreational drugs, alcohol, or new medications, or do you have any medical conditions like thyroid issues that started around the same time as these symptoms?
No, I don't use any recreational drugs, and I rarely drink alcohol. I'm not taking any new medications, and as far as I know, I don't have any medical conditions like thyroid issues.
When you have those periods of feeling wired and high-energy, how long does a single one of those phases typically last continuously—is it usually a few days, a week, or even longer?

I'm not entirely sure of the exact number of days or weeks that each individual high-energy phase lasts continuously. I just know that these wired periods have been coming and going for about a year and eight months now.
During those times when you felt wired and full of energy, did it ever lead to hospitalization, or cause major disruptions in your daily life and relationships?

No, I’ve never been hospitalized, but those high-energy periods have caused major disruptions in my life. I start a dozen projects and leave them unfinished, let bills pile up, and miss appointments, which has really strained my relationships with my family. It's even caused me to withdraw from my life and stop going to my book club.
During those times when you feel wired and high-energy, does that feeling typically last continuously for at least a week, or is it usually shorter, lasting only a few days?

I'm not entirely sure of the exact number of days because I tend to lose track of time when I'm in those wired phases. However, they definitely feel like they go on for quite a while, rather than just lasting a few days.
Have you ever experienced times where you felt highly energetic and wired, but at the very same time felt deeply sad, empty, or hopeless?

No, I don't experience those two states at the same time; they happen in completely separate phases. I will have periods where I am wired, fast-talking, and full of high energy, and then other entirely different times where I feel heavy, sad, and empty.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a history of both manic episodes (characterized by high energy, decreased need for sleep, pressured speech, and goal-directed hyperactivity causing functional impairment) and depressive episodes (characterized by flat affect, emptiness, and loss of interest), occurring alongside persistent psychotic symptoms. The psychotic symptoms include auditory hallucinations (voices commenting on her parenting), referential delusions (believing her family is testing her), and disorganized speech. Crucially, these psychotic symptoms persisted for a 2-to-3-week period during which her mood was completely stable and neutral. Because she has experienced both manic and depressive mood phases in addition to the persistent schizophrenic-like symptoms, she meets the criteria for Schizoaffective disorder, mixed type (F25.2).
